title: 2025 AMC 10B Problem 11
statement: On Monday, \(6\) students went to the tutoring center at the same time, and each one was randomly assigned to one of the \(6\) tutors on duty. On Tuesday, the same \(6\) students showed up, the same \(6\) tutors were on duty, and the students were again randomly assigned to the tutors. What is the probability that exactly \(2\) students met with the same tutor both Monday and Tuesday?

solutions.text: Each day’s assignment is a permutation of the \(6\) students among the \(6\) tutors. Comparing the two days, the number who keep the same tutor is the number of fixed points of \(\tau = \pi_{\text{Tue}}^{-1}\pi_{\text{Mon}},\) itself a uniformly random permutation of \(6\) elements. We want exactly \(2\) fixed points, so choose those \(2\) in \(\binom{6}{2}\) ways and derange the other \(4,\) where \(D_4 = 9.\) The probability is \(\dfrac{\binom{6}{2} D_4}{6!} = \dfrac{15 \cdot 9}{720} = \dfrac{3}{16}.\) Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Each day’s assignment is a permutation; comparing the two days is like a single random permutation, and “same tutor” means a fixed point
Choose the \(2\) matched students in \(\binom{6}{2}\) ways and derange the other \(4\) (there are \(D_4 = 9\) derangements); divide by \(6!\)
